Store each item with a unique, immutable Item ID in the format MTMH_NNN. Existing IDs MTMH_101 to MTMH_203 are preserved exactly; new items take the next free number (MTMH_204 onward); IDs are never reused, even after an item is retired.
Each item has Item name, Model number, Type, Brand, Serial number, Owner, Status, Condition, Current holder, Home location, Stock image, Latest photo and Notes (see section 6).

Type is a controlled list derived from the sheet: Camera, Lens, Audio, Light, Light accessory, Accessory, Tripod, Stand, Reflector, Backdrop, SD Card, Battery, Drone. Managers can add a value; the Owner approves new values.

Support an optional Subtype for the 44 items typed Accessory (for example Bag or case, Charger, Card reader, Filter, Rig part, Clamp, Gimbal, Monitor) so lists can be filtered without changing the sheet Type.

Support two quantity modes: Single (one tagged physical unit, for example MTMH_101 Sony FX3) and Counted (a quantity of identical units, for example MTMH_191 Small Spring Clamps pack of 20, MTMH_141 Sony NP-FZ100 batteries, stock 6).
For Counted items, track quantity per holder and per status (for example MTMH_110 E-Image tripod: 1 with Madtown, 1 with Kittu) instead of a comma-separate d holder field.
Allow a Counted item to be split into Single units later, each with its own ID or a unit suffix, without losing history (Siddharth to propose the suffix format, see section 14).
Record Owner separately from Current holder. Default Owner is Madtown. Items owned by a person (for example MTMH_115, owned by Anand) are excluded from Madtown asset value reports.
Allow Model number to be blank or TBD with a flag, and show a To verify list (for example MTMH_202 Lighting Umbrella: TBD, Naveen to provide).
Provide search by ID, name, model number, type, holder, status and condition, with results in under 1 second for the full catalog.
Provide filters and saved views: Out now, Overdue, In repair, Lost, Missing, Bad condition, Owned by others, Missing photos, To verify.

Record purchase details where known: purchase date, vendor, order number, price, invoice file, warranty end (for example MTMH_203: Kamal Imaging, order KI/SO/30101, 19 Sep 2026, Rs 21,999 incl GST). Price fields are hidden from Team members.
Allow an item to be retired, sold or written off with a reason and Owner approval; retired items stay searchable but are excluded from active counts.
Keep the original sheet row number and original raw values for each imported item for traceability.

Show a To verify flag with reason on items whose stock, model or details are unconfirmed (for example MTMH_197 Sony BC-QZ1 charger: stock of 3 is TO VERIFY; MTMH_198 to MTMH_201 need details from Anand).
Generate one QR code per item and per kit, encoding a short URL in the form inventory.madto wn.in/i/MTMH_1 01 (domain to be confirmed).
Scanning with the phone camera opens the item page; an in-app scan button opens the camera directly.
The item page shows the current status and the correct primary action (Check out, Check in, Report issue).
Provide a Print labels page that outputs a printable sheet of QR labels with ID and name, for selected or new items, sized for 25 mm by 25 mm durable labels.
Support labelling the pouch, case or kit for tiny items (lens caps, cables, filters) instead of the item itself.
Fallback search by typed ID or name when a label is worn or missing.

Support a parent item link so an accessory belongs to a main item (for example MTMH_163 SmallRig Cage for FX3 belongs to MTMH_101 Sony FX3; MTMH_158 Digitex F750 Battery relates to MTMH_159 Smart Pro F750 Battery Charger).

Support kits: a named group of items with a contents list, each part keeping its own ID (for example DJI RS4 Pro Combo Gimbal MTMH_182 with MTMH_183 BG70 battery grip and MTMH_184 Twist Grip; Godox SA projection set MTMH_168 to MTMH_178).
Each kit line has a quantity and a Required flag (required parts block a complete check-in; optional parts warn).
A kit can be checked out and checked in as one unit; the check-in shows a checklist of its contents.
Record Missing part entries against a parent item (for example MTMH_109 DJI Mic 2: charging cable missing) and link them to a to-buy item.
Record detached accessories held by someone else (for example MTMH_119 AD600 PRO battery and charger with Anand for timely charging) without marking the parent as checked out.

Record the case or bag an item travels in as a link to a case item (for example MTMH_138 DJI Air 2S now carried in a smaller camera bag; MTMH_190 Ulanzi Hard Shell Camera Bag; MTMH_189 Magic line Photo Studio Trolley Case).
Store case capacity notes (for example the Mobius Chrom stand bag holds 2 Harison stands, not 4) and flag items with no case (for example MTMH_120 Godox QT600 III used from retail boxes).
Show on the parent item page all children, kit memberships and missing parts.
Check-out: scan or select an item or kit, choose borrower (default: logged-in user), purpose or project, due date, condition at check-out and photos, then save. Status becomes Checked out.
Default due dates by Type (Sheldon Cooper proposes 2 days for cameras and 7 days for tripods); defaults are editable by the Owner.
At least one check-out photo is required for Camera, Lens and Drone items; optional for others (final list per section 14).
Check-in: scan, the app shows the open loan, user takes photos, confirms accessories present, sets condition and adds notes. Status becomes Available, or In repair if damage is reported.
If condition at check-in is worse than at check-out, the app prompts to open a repair or incident record in one tap and links it to the loan.
Block a second check-out of a Single item that is already checked out; for Counted items block check-out beyond available quantity.
Warn when the borrower already has overdue items; a Manager can override with a recorded reason.
Allow transfer from one holder to another in one step (for example Anand to a freelancer) so the chain of custody is unbroken.
Allow due date extension with a reason.
Allow a Manager to record a loan for a borrower without login (for example Chiru) with optional phone and email.
Allow partial check-in for Counted items and kits (for example 2 of 3 MTMH_145 cards returned) with the remainder left open or reported lost.
Allow reservations for a future shoot date so two people do not plan the same item.
Record check-out and check-in times automatically in IST, and the user who performed each action.
Allow back-dated check-in by a Manager with a reason (for example MTMH_103 returned by Chiru on 16 Oct 2026, not 15 Oct).
Store every loan as its own record (one row per loan) so full history survives; the item page shows the last 20 loans and a link to all.
Loan status values: Open, Returned, Overdue, Lost (see section 6).
Send reminders: due soon (24 hours before), due today, overdue daily until returned.
Escalate overdue loans to Anand and Naveen after 3 days overdue (per Technical input: Sheldon Cooper; Naveen to confirm).
Phase 1 reminders by email; Slack alerts in Phase 2; WhatsApp in Phase 3 through Graham Bell.
Borrower profile shows open loans, overdue loans, loan history and items returned damaged.
Record legacy loans found in notes at migration as closed or open historical loans (for example MTMH_126 loaned to Purushotham about a year ago, open until Naveen confirms with Purushotham).
Allow a Manager to mark an open loan as Lost which opens a Lost incident linked to the borrower.
Record the project or shoot for each loan (free text in Phase 1; linked project code in Phase 3).
Count reminders sent per loan and show them on the loan.
Keep Condition separate from Status. Condition values derived from the sheet: Good, Bad condition (Sheldon Cooper proposes Fair and New as additions; see section 14).
Record maintenance events with type (Service, Repair, Cleaning, Calibration, Firmware), issue, reported by, reported date, vendor, date sent, expected back, date returned, cost, invoice, outcome.
Maintenance event states: Reported, Sent for repair, In repair, Returned, Closed.
While an item has an open repair, its Status is In repair and it cannot be checked out (for example MTMH_106 Sony 16-35mm G-Master).
Record the cause of damage where known (for example MTMH_106: lens cells shifted inside the carrier in transit) and link to any loan.
Support upkeep schedules per item or Type (for example service every 6 months for cameras, per Sheldon Cooper) with reminders to Anand.
Show a timeline per item: loans, repairs, incidents, photos, audits.
Convert the existing service note Serviced on 14th July into a Service event during migration, with the year flagged To verify.
Report total cost of ownership per item (purchase price plus repairs).
Allow flagging replaceable defects (for example MTMH_132 to MTMH_135 NISI UV filters heavily scratched) and create a linked to-buy item in one step.

Distinguish Lost (confirmed lost, for example MTMH_123 Godox QR-P120 Softbox, lost during the Dasara shoot) from Missing (whereabouts unknown, being searched, for example the GoPro in Not yet sorted: Missing: to locate).
Record an incident with type (Damage, Loss, Theft, Found), description, reported by, date, last known holder, last seen location and linked loan.
Allow unknown history to be recorded explicitly (for example MTMH_111 Fotopro Predator Tripod: how and when unknown) rather than leaving fields blank.
For partial losses in Counted items, record the quantity lost and the person responsible where known (for example MTMH_145: one card lost at Shorefest by Samuel).
Missing items generate a weekly reminder to the Manager until resolved.
Resolution options: Found, Written off (Owner approval), Insurance claim, Replaced (link to to-buy item).
Found flow: scanning a tagged item that is Lost or Missing prompts the user to mark it found, records where and by whom, and notifies the Manager.
Lost items stay in the catalog with status Lost and are excluded from available counts and asset value.
Maintain a to-buy list with item, reason, related item IDs (one or many), replaces or adds, priority, status, estimated cost, options researched, links and notes (mirrors the To buy tab).
To-buy statuses: To research, To buy (both from the sheet), then Approved, Ordered, Received, Rejected (from Technical input: Sheldon Cooper).
Priority values from the sheet: High, Medium, Low.
Replaces or adds values from the sheet: Replaces, Adds, and combined values (for example Replaces (case) and adds (missing accessories) for MTMH_116), stored as a primary value plus a note.
Approval: Managers propose, the Owner approves or rejects with a comment; the approver and time are recorded.

Record incoming orders: vendor, order number, order date, amount, GST invoice or order PDF, expected delivery, delivery date, and cancelled orders (for example MTMH_203: order KI/SO/30093 cancelled, order KI/SO/30101 confirmed).
On Received, create the new item records in one step with new MTMH IDs, link them to the order and the to-buy line, and prompt for stock photo and QR label.
Show to-buy lines on the related item page (for example the Pelican 1510 hard case line on MTMH_106).
Support verify before buy lines (for example MTMH_197 BC-QZ1 charger: confirm count with Anand first, then buy up to 3).
Store multiple researched options per line with vendor, price and stock note (for example DJI Air 2S battery: Pooja Electronics, Flyworldgadget, Design Info).
Each item has two primary photo fields: Stock image (clean product shot, from the sheet Links column) and Latest photo (most recent real photo, from the Updated links column).
Keep photo history: operational photos are stored with kind (Stock, Latest, Check-out, Check-in, Damage, Invoice), taken by and taken at.
Capture photos from the phone camera inside the app, compress on the device (about 1600 px longest side) and upload in the background.
Store photo files in Madtown-owned Google Drive, one folder per item; store only the Drive file ID and a thumbnail reference in the database (Technical input: Sheldon Cooper).
A new check-in photo can be promoted to Latest photo; the previous Latest photo stays in history.
Flag items with missing or invalid photos (for example MTMH_187 has neither photo; Updated links holds the text lost or Need replacement on 11 rows).
Handle stock links that point to a Drive folder instead of a file (MTMH_101, 102, 103, 110, 112, 119) by letting a Manager pick the stock image from the folder.
Use a storage adapter so Drive can be replaced by another store (Supabase Storage or Cloudflare R2) without data changes.
